items.text: A video sent to Iran International from Iranshahr in Sistan and Baluchestan province shows a long line of vehicles waiting for fuel at 4:30 AM on Sunday, 24 Aban.

Miad Maleki, former head of the Targeting Office of the US Treasury Department, said about Mossad's warning to Washington regarding the Islamic Republic's plan to target Donald Trump and senior officials of his administration: "These threats make the US government more determined to increase pressure on the Islamic Republic, and Trump will finish the Islamic Republic's work in the next two years."

The Islamic Republic's renewed attack on Bahrain has faced regional condemnation. Qatar's Foreign Ministry described the attack as a factor weakening diplomatic efforts. The Wall Street Journal reported that US intelligence agencies estimate the Islamic Republic has between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles, which would provide significant capability to strike American and allied targets if war resumes.

Informed sources told Iran International that prisoners in Ward 4, Unit 6 of Tehran's Great Prison face severe food shortages, unsanitary conditions, and limited access to showers. Many of these prisoners are detainees from the January protests. The population of this ward is estimated to be between 360 and 400 people.

In recent years, reports have emerged about the assassination, kidnapping, and interrogation of IRGC members by Mossad. The New York Times, in an investigative report, covered Mossad and the Israeli government's efforts to clarify the fate of Ron Arad, an Israeli pilot missing since October 1986, and details of the kidnapping of two senior IRGC commanders by Mossad. An interview was conducted with Ashkan Safaei, a reporter for Iran International.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations regarding the non-use of children in military affairs, 1,281 students from various counties were sent to operational areas as part of the Rahian-e Noor tours. Also, an official from the Ministry of Education announced that this year, 250,000 students from across the country will be sent to operational areas in the south and northwest of the country with the participation of the Ministry of Education and the Student Basij Organization.

Nazanin Abedini, a Baháʼí citizen residing in Qaemshahr, was sentenced by the Sari Revolutionary Court to three years in prison and eight years of deprivation of social rights. She was charged with propaganda against the Islamic Republic system and propaganda in favor of groups opposing the system. The court considered her educational and religious activities, including teaching Baháʼí beliefs to children, as falling under Article 500 bis of the Islamic Penal Code and issued her sentence accordingly.

Abbas Mousavi, acting deputy of the political office of the presidency, stated that Mostafa Pourmohammadi is among the government's candidates for the Ministry of Intelligence and that the selection requires consensus. He mentioned that some names like Mohammad Sadegh Motamedian and Alireza Rashidian might not be considered by government committees. Mousavi described the Ministry of Intelligence as sensitive and emphasized it must be managed without factional disputes.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said the Islamic Consultative Assembly, by approving an urgent plan to reform the structure of the Ministry of Intelligence, seeks to reduce the government's powers and increase Mojtaba Khamenei's direct control over intelligence institutions. According to this plan, two organizations of Information Protection and Political-Ideological will be formed, whose heads will be directly appointed by the Supreme Leader. These organizations, by supervising the performance of the minister and employees of the Ministry of Intelligence, will weaken the minister's position and transfer control of the ministry from the government to the Supreme Leader.

At least 9 protest gatherings were held on Sunday, 24 Aban. Truck drivers in Rafsanjan protested in front of the city’s Friday Imam office. Social Security retirees also gathered in several cities including Shush, Rasht, Kermanshah, Tehran, and Ahvaz.
A man in Tehran accused of killing his wife and 12-year-old daughter was tried today in Branch 10 of the criminal court of this province.

Three days after Trump said he no longer wants an agreement with the Islamic Republic, Qalibaf warned that Tehran will not accept a state of neither war nor peace. An hour ago, the IRGC attacked Bahrain with a drone; a step towards a preemptive attack, while Netanyahu has called for an immediate attack on Iran.

Nejat Bahrami said the Islamic Republic's renewed attack on Bahrain is an attempt to exit the state of neither war nor peace and to end pressures from the American blockade. He added that Tehran aims to increase tensions by targeting regional infrastructure and push the US to start a new round of war. Bahrami believes that continued missile attacks and increased US military readiness will make a broad conflict inevitable.

Marca reported that the match between Ravenna and Forlì, the Emilia-Romagna derby, became the most viewed match in the history of Italy's Serie C. The reason for this attention was Ronaldinho's return to professional football, 11 years after retiring. Ronaldinho returned to the pitch on November 15, 2026, at the Bruno Benelli stadium and played for more than half an hour.

Investigations by Iran International show that Hossein Yazdankhah, head of the fifth branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, has played a role in issuing death sentences for several December protesters and sentencing lawyers and political prisoners. He has issued death sentences for at least 11 detainees from the December protests and has been involved in cases such as the conviction of Fatemeh Sepahri and the confiscation of Marzieh Mohabi's assets. Despite this record, his name is not on the individual sanctions lists of the US, UK, or the European Union.
Niusha Saremi reported in the audio version of Titrawol that Mossad warned about Tehran's plan to assassinate Trump. It was also reported that the US and Europe are on security alert.

Videos received by Iran International show a group of Iranians residing in the UK in the cities of London and Sheffield in England and Glasgow in Scotland, taking to the streets against the Islamic Republic.
It was reported that Mojtaba Khamenei took the first step to seize the Ministry of Intelligence.

Leila Morvati, a political analyst, said political and economic monopoly, suppression of protests, and military expenses have caused a deep economic crisis for the Islamic Republic. She added that the government struggles to meet the economic needs of its middle layers and economic decline has surpassed political decline. Morvati also said regional tensions continue and Republican disagreements do not mean the military option is off the table.

Narges Mohammadi, Nobel Peace Prize laureate, criticized the ongoing repression of writers, poets, and journalists in Iran on her Instagram, mentioning arrests, trials, and sentences including death penalties. She referred to the retrial of five journalists and poets in Abadan and the referral of death sentence for imprisoned songwriter Peyman Farahavar to the enforcement branch. Mohammadi also mentioned the treatment of several writers and prison sentences for others, emphasizing the importance of supporting imprisoned writers.

Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst, said the Islamic Republic government is implementing a broad plan to eliminate energy subsidies with a focus on combating fuel smuggling. She added that a large part of fuel smuggling is organized and the cost of combating it falls on the people and drivers. Taherkhani warned that calculating gasoline prices based on dollar rates could greatly increase economic pressure and inflation.

The Iranian Writers' Association reported on the World Day of Imprisoned Writers that at least 20 writers and poets are imprisoned or detained, and one imprisoned writer faces the risk of execution. The association stated that after the suppression of the protests in Dey 1404 and the war of the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic, a climate of intimidation and censorship has prevailed in the country. They also warned about the risk of execution of Peyman Farahavar.

Ghassan Ashour, a Middle East analyst, said the Iraqi government is trying to reduce the influence of armed groups close to the Islamic Republic by pursuing the oil smuggling case in the Jurf al-Sakhar area. He added that exposing the illegal activities of these groups could reduce political support for them and pave the way for disarmament or limiting their presence. Ashour also said that the income from oil smuggling does not only benefit Iraqi armed groups, but some officials in Iran and Turkey also profit from this network.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the largest gathering of US aircraft carriers in the Middle East in the past 23 years includes three aircraft carriers, more than 20 destroyers, and about 150 warplanes. He added that with the arrival of the Roosevelt carrier to the CENTCOM region, the US military posture against the Islamic Republic has reached its highest level. Also, 200 refueling aircraft are ready to support American and Israeli fighters, and he questioned whether Trump is on the verge of issuing an attack order.

The Belgium national football team defeated Italy 4-1 in the last group stage match of the UEFA Nations League and advanced to the quarter-finals as the second team in Group 1 of League A with 12 points. Italy was eliminated with this loss. In another match of the group, France beat Turkey 2-1 and topped the group with 13 points.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, compared the leaders of the Islamic Republic to rats trapped in sewers who are unaware of the people's situation in underground shelters. Bessent said the situation in Iran is rapidly changing. At the same time, Mike Pence, former Vice President under Trump, emphasized the US military superiority in the previous war and called the ceasefire with the Islamic Republic a mistake.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that with the loss of about one-third of the country's gas production due to the IRGC's war policies, the gas shortage crisis has intensified. He added that even a complete cut of gas to industries may not meet the gas needs of households. Concerns about cutting household gas during the peak of winter cold have also increased.

Meysam Mehrani, a political analyst, said Tehran is seeking to use proxy networks and aligned groups worldwide by expanding threats beyond the region. He considered this situation a result of years of US and European appeasement policies toward the Islamic Republic. Mehrani added that the positions of Islamic Republic officials about readiness for negotiation and threats of retaliatory actions should not be seen as contradictory, stating that the Foreign Ministry, Parliament, and military and security institutions act within a common policy framework.

Kamyar Behrang, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the plan to remove the requirement of Ijtihad for the Minister of Intelligence and to form two organizations for intelligence protection and ideological-political affairs means expanding parallel security work within the Ministry of Intelligence. According to him, the heads of these two organizations will be directly under Mojtaba Khamenei, the leader of the Islamic Republic, and these changes could further limit the powers of the Minister of Intelligence. Behrang added that instead of examining the reasons for Israeli intelligence infiltration and weaknesses in security structures, the Islamic Republic continues to focus on ideological loyalty and a record of repression in selecting intelligence officials, and the ability to counter security infiltration is not a priority.

Thomas Tuchel, head coach of the England national team, said after the difficult 3-2 victory against Spain that his team showed their best performance since he started coaching. He added that the red card and penalty changed the match and that the victory was deserved. Tuchel emphasized that the team is progressing and does not want to retreat after achieving this style of play.

Luis de la Fuente, Spain's coach, said after a 3-2 loss to England that nothing special happens and his team will return in March with renewed energy to reach the Nations League final again and strive for the championship. He added the match was very close, his team had many chances, and he is proud to be the coach. De la Fuente emphasized the journey continues and Spain still has a chance to win the Nations League.

The Iranian national football team defeated Palestine 2-0 in their first match at the Iraq tournament. Amir Ghalenoei sent the national team with young players to this game; the average age of the national team in this game was more than 4 years younger than the previous FIFA date and the match against Russia.

Barak Ravid, Axios reporter, on Sunday 24 Aban reported quoting a US official that the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt has entered the operational area of the US Central Command, CENTCOM. The CENTCOM operational area includes the Middle East and parts of Central and South Asia. With the arrival of the Theodore Roosevelt, there are now three US aircraft carrier strike groups in the region.

The US Embassy in Bahrain issued a security warning on Sunday, November 15, urging American citizens to be more vigilant due to increased threats from Houthi attacks supported by the Islamic Republic and Tehran's efforts to target US officials and facilities in the region. This warning came after a new round of attacks on Bahrain, home to the US Fifth Fleet. The Revolutionary Guard claimed to have targeted a US radar facility with six drones.

On Saturday, several former Iranian football players attended the burial site of Hassan Nasrallah and received a trophy. Meanwhile, despite 10 months passing since 18 and 19 Dey, the people of Iran are still mourning.

Ahmad Bigdeli, a member of the Social Commission of the Parliament, said that military and law enforcement forces are in their worst living conditions. He also pointed to the livelihood problems of teachers, farmers, and workers and said the current salaries do not meet their living expenses. Bigdeli called on the government to take action to improve the living conditions of these groups.

A group of Iranians residing in Calgary, Canada, gathered in front of the city hall as part of their weekly protests, supporting Fatemeh Sepahri, a political prisoner, and commemorating the victims of the November 2019 protests. Participants also paid tribute to Kianoush Sanjari, a political activist, on the second anniversary of his death.

The French government announced that a cyber unit affiliated with the IRGC was involved in attacks on the cooling systems of more than 700 stores in the country. According to the French government, these attacks caused large amounts of food to spoil and resulted in multi-million euro damages.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher, said the arrival of the aircraft carrier group Theodore Roosevelt to the CENTCOM region increases the operational capability of the US to attack Iran. He also said Donald Trump faces a time constraint between continuing economic pressure on the Islamic Republic to gain diplomatic concessions and returning to the military option.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, said that the disputes over the selection of the Minister of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic indicate the limited role of Mojtaba Khamenei and the dominance of the security Sepah coalition over the power structure. He added that this coalition is unwilling to strengthen the Ministry of Intelligence and increase the institutional powers outside the Sepah, and the disputes over the minister's selection are a sign of crisis and declining trust in the government's security structure.

Leaders of Southeast Asian countries have started the three-day ASEAN summit in Manila. Associated Press reported that the Middle East war and its consequences are at the top of the agenda. Donald Trump and Marco Rubio are scheduled to travel to Manila on Tuesday, November 17, to meet with ASEAN leaders.

Mohammad Zahraei, head of the Basij Construction Organization, announced the launch of a campaign to collect two million livelihood packages with public participation. The plan depends on the financial and voluntary participation of citizens to provide necessary aid to needy families. He also announced a program to collect 168,000 stationery items, bags, and shoes in memory of the victims of Minab and 21,000 other items in memory of the victims of Lamerd.

The Public Relations of the IRGC Navy announced early Monday, 25 Aban, that two tankers hit naval mines while passing through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz, exploded, and caught fire. According to the IRGC, the number of tankers that have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz since Sunday, 24 Aban, has reached six. The IRGC Navy also wrote that pollution caused by the tanker explosions has spread in the waters of the Strait of Hormuz.

Kayhan newspaper wrote on 25 Aban that the Trump administration, instead of focusing on the economy and internal infrastructure, has wasted the country's energy in costly wars with the Islamic Republic. The newspaper also described the crisis at US airports as a sign of structural decline in the country and pointed to the technological incapacity of the US in managing domestic flights.

Nezameddin Misaghi, an anesthesiology specialist and university assistant professor, pointed to a fourfold increase in the price of blood sugar test strips in Iran. He said reduced access for diabetic patients to these strips makes blood sugar control and treatment adjustment difficult and can increase the risk of serious complications including kidney damage, vision problems, and heart and brain diseases. He also cited lack of transparency in the import, production, and distribution of medicine in the Islamic Republic as a factor that could worsen shortages of equipment and medicine.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, said at the ECO summit in Pakistan that the land, airspace, and facilities of regional countries should not become a platform for attacks against each other. He added that Tehran's defensive actions are solely directed at the military targets of aggressors and should not be considered actions against the people or governments of neighboring countries. Araghchi also stated that sanctions have not weakened Iran's resolve but strengthened its determination to defend its rights, and he identified the policies of the United States and Israel as causes of insecurity in the Persian Gulf.

Kazem Jalali, the ambassador of the Islamic Republic in Moscow, said that Mojtaba Khamenei's message to Putin was a special message and indicated the continuation of consultations at the highest level. Jalali emphasized that the main purpose of Mohsen Rezaei's trip to Moscow was to deliver this message. He added that this trip should be evaluated within the framework of strategic relations and continuous consultations at the highest level between the Islamic Republic and Russia.

Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations, called for the start of a serious diplomatic process and negotiations to end the current situation between Iran and the United States. He said that to end the neither peace nor war status between the US and Iran, a serious diplomatic process is needed. Guterres also announced that the United Nations is ready to fully cooperate in any initiative for nuclear disarmament involving the US, China, and Russia.
Counterattacks between Russia and Ukraine have intensified. In recent Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy and railway infrastructure, at least three people were killed and more than 30 were injured.

Economic pressure in Iran has driven some citizens to sell their body parts to pay debts and cover living expenses and their children's future. Iran International's investigation shows this market is no longer limited to kidney sales, and in one-third of the ads reviewed, multiple body parts or tissues were simultaneously offered for sale.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a long line of cars waiting for gasoline at midnight on Sunday, 24 Aban. The citizen said the line was so long that they regretted refueling.

Rouhollah Rahimpour, a journalist and political analyst, said the entry of the aircraft carrier Theodore Roosevelt into the CENTCOM region and the increase of US aircraft carriers to three is a political message to the Islamic Republic and a sign of the completion of the US military posture for a possible start of war. He added that if the war restarts, the Islamic Republic will attack regional countries, especially those in the Persian Gulf; however, the expansion of the conflict to Europe and outside the Middle East is not certain.

Despite reports about the opening of Esteghlal's transfer window, a review of FIFA's transfer system shows that the club's ban remains in place and Esteghlal's window has not opened. Since Sunday, rumors about lifting Esteghlal's transfer ban have circulated, but according to ISNA, a technical issue in FIFA's official website database caused these reports. Esteghlal has been banned from two transfer windows by FIFA since last winter due to a complaint by Montazer Mohammed and some contract termination cases.

The Tehran Provincial Court of Appeal confirmed the prison sentence of Arman Misaghian, a Baháʼí citizen. He was sentenced to two years of imprisonment for charges of propaganda against the regime and insulting the leadership. Additionally, he was banned for two years from driving, signing commercial documents, and membership in groups.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced on Monday, 25 Aban, that an oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile while exiting the Strait of Hormuz. The organization added that the projectile caused a fire in the engine room of the tanker, but the extent of damage and environmental consequences are still unknown. No casualties were reported and the crew's status is confirmed.

Alireza Salimi, a member of the parliament's presidium, said the time for pleading with Americans has passed and the Islamic Republic is stronger today. He added that we stand powerfully and have the Americans by the throat. Salimi also said European countries and the US face serious economic challenges.

BBC Sport reported that the England national football team defeated Spain 3-2 with a defensive performance in the final minutes and topped their group in the UEFA Nations League. This victory came after the bitter experience of losing to Argentina in the World Cup. Thomas Tuchel, despite a player being sent off, used a different strategy in managing substitutions.

A released video shows the principal of the "Mahd Elm" school in the city of Riz, Bushehr province, forcing a student to throw their mobile phone into a bucket of water. After the student refuses, the principal hits the student's hand and throws the phone into the bucket, which causes injury to the student.

Homayoun Sameyh Najafabadi, a member of the Health and Treatment Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, reported a shortage of foreign currency for medicine and medical equipment and increased pressure on treatment costs. He said financial inability to buy medicine has reached northern Tehran. It was also reported that despite allocating three billion dollars of preferential currency for medicine and medical equipment in last year's budget, there is a shortage of 500 to 700 million dollars, and the government has not yet taken specific action to provide the needed currency.

Jude Bellingham and Marc Cucurella, two Real Madrid players, had a severe verbal altercation during the England vs Spain match at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. The altercation started after a penalty incident leading to England's first goal and continued during the match. Despite the tensions, the two players shook hands after the final whistle and ended their dispute.

Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations, said at a press conference on November 16 in Manila that the UN has condemned the killing of protesters on January 9 and 10. He added that the UN does not have the tools to stop these actions but has raised the issue of the death penalty with the President of Iran. Guterres emphasized that the UN will continue to firmly demand respect for human rights in Iran and worldwide.

Arman Mardani, a citizen from Kamyaran County, was arrested on 21 Aban after being summoned to the Intelligence Department. He was transferred to one of the detention centers of the Sanandaj Intelligence Department.
A video sent to Iran International shows a queue of cars waiting to receive gasoline in front of a fuel station in Chitgar, Tehran, on the evening of Sunday, 24 Aban.
A man in Tehran was killed by his wife through poisoning. The suspect has been arrested by the police.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, participated in the ECO summit in Islamabad. After the meeting of the ECO foreign ministers, he said the summit showed a good reaction to the current situation in the region and welcomed the Islamic Republic's proposed two-day plan to end the war with the United States.

Mohammad Jafar Asadi, former deputy inspector of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said the enemy does not only use mobile phones to collect information, and surveillance cameras and artificial intelligence systems also analyze data. He added that citizens' information is recorded in various systems and data traces remain wherever they are present. Asadi also mentioned that people themselves are providing services and information, and there is no place left to hide.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the issue of Iran will be an important topic in the meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping in China. He added that Russia and China want a diplomatic resolution to the war but do not want to lose their geopolitical influence in Iran. Aghaei emphasized that Trump should not agree to maintain Beijing and Moscow's influence in Iran if he pursues regime change in Iran.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, wrote on Network X on Tuesday, 25 Aban, that the case known as "the refrigerators" in France and the "allegation of assassination attempts on American officials" is a maliciously organized narrative by Israeli media and psychological warfare apparatus. Baqaei added that the goal is to portray the Islamic Republic not only as a threat to Western governments but also as an enemy of ordinary people and their daily lives. The spokesperson continued that American officials taking refuge in military shelters after claiming victory in the war is an obvious attempt to gain public sympathy, whose minds are angry at their leaders' lies and the transformation of the US into a tool for advancing Israel's priorities.

Israel's security cabinet held a three-hour meeting to discuss developments related to Iran and the military readiness of the US and Israel in the region. This was the first security cabinet meeting in Israel in 40 days. Channel 11 Israel reported that the Israeli army and CENTCOM are on maximum alert regarding developments in Iran.

The Supreme Court rejected the appeal request of Javad Alikardi, a detained lawyer in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, and confirmed the previous sentences against him. Abbas Mousavi, his defense lawyer, stated that the Supreme Court rejected the request for retrial and upheld the sentences of imprisonment, exile, disbarment, and travel ban.

A citizen sent a message to Iran International about the November 2019 killings by the Islamic Republic, saying: "We were supposed to honk in the streets to protest, but the government carried out a massacre. For me, who remembered the 2009 crimes, it was not strange, but for many, the regime's hand was revealed. Although for some, even seeing the 2025 massacre has not yet revealed the regime's hand."

The Football Federation Appeals Committee rejected Gol Gohar's complaint about Yaser Asani's presence in Esteghlal's lineup, confirmed the disciplinary committee's ruling, and closed the case. Gol Gohar claimed Asani had terminated his contract with Esteghlal and his return was illegal due to the closed transfer window. The Appeals Committee stated that Asani's contract termination was never registered and his playing license remained valid.

Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, in response to a question from an Iran International reporter about the killing of protesters on 18 and 19 Dey, emphasized that this issue has been condemned by the United Nations and called the human rights violations in Iran unacceptable.

The prison sentences of Amirhossein Mohseni-Pour, Mehdi Karami, and Milad Karimi-Nasab, three political prisoners in Dehdasht prison, have been converted to open verdicts. These individuals will serve the remainder of their sentences outside prison and are required to report daily to the prison and register their presence. According to the HRANA news agency, these three prisoners have been released from Dehdasht prison.

Mohammadreza Ahmadi Sangar, representative of Rasht in the parliament, said that the Islamic Republic will not dilute its 400 kilograms of uranium and will continue 60 percent enrichment. He added that 60 percent enrichment will be used for treating diseases and supplying the country's energy needs. Ahmadi Sangar emphasized that the Islamic Republic decides the level and percentage of enrichment and will no longer wait for threats from the US.

Mostafa Ramazani, a political prisoner in Qezel Hesar prison, announced in an audio message that he will start a wet hunger strike from November 14 to November 24 and an unlimited dry hunger strike from November 25. This hunger strike is in protest against the executions by the Islamic Republic.

On Monday, 25 Aban, a group of retired telecommunications workers held a protest in the cities of Kermanshah, Sanandaj, and Bijar. The protesting retirees stated that addressing livelihood and healthcare issues was among their demands.

A video on social media shows that the principal of Mahd Elm School in Riz, Bushehr, after a student refused to throw his mobile phone into a bucket of water, hit the student's hand and threw the phone into the bucket. The images indicate injury to the student's hand.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Trump administration currently has intensifying economic pressure and isolation of the Islamic Republic on its agenda, and the simultaneous increase of US military presence in the region also maintains a shadow of military threat over the regime. According to him, Trump, with this strategy, alongside pressure on the regime, is waiting for the economic and social consequences inside Iran and the people's reaction to the current conditions.

France announced that on Monday it will present evidence of a cyberattack attributed to the IRGC targeting refrigerators in food stores in the country to European ministers and will call for new sanctions against Tehran. Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said Paris aims to prepare a list of new individuals and entities for sanctions within a month.

Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, criticized the negotiation plan with the US, saying it does not specify who the "aggressor" is. He questioned whether the death of Ali Khamenei was accidental or an act of aggression. Nabavian added that without identifying the aggressor, the cases of punishing the aggressor and revenge will be closed, and he asked officials why they no longer talk about revenge.
A video published on social media shows that rainfall caused flooding and the entry of floodwaters into Mazgah village in Nowshahr on Monday, 25 Aban.

Romelu Lukaku, the 33-year-old striker of the Belgium national team and Fenerbahçe club, suddenly announced his retirement from international football after 16 years. He wrote on Instagram that he enjoyed every moment of this adventure and thanked his teammates, coaches, and fans. Lukaku ended his international career with 135 appearances and 94 goals, becoming the top scorer in Belgium's national team history.
Today, continuing the gatherings of telecommunications retirees; some of these retirees in the cities of Tehran and Isfahan also held a protest gathering demanding attention to their demands.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Monday, 25 Aban, showing a queue of cars waiting for gasoline on one of the roads leading to Bushehr, stating that most gas stations did not have gasoline cards and only one station had one card.
A video sent to Iran International on Monday, 25 Aban, shows severe air pollution in Tehran. According to the video, a thick black haze has enveloped the city like a shadow.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said France was likely targeted by a cyberattack on cooling systems in stores because it has consistently supported the Iranian people against the Islamic Republic's repression. He held the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responsible and said France submitted files with evidence about the main perpetrators to the European Union, requesting sanctions within one month. Barrot added that broad support was gained at the EU foreign ministers' meeting for these sanctions and he hopes they will be approved at the December 14 meeting.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said many of his counterparts in the European Union support new sanctions. He described these sanctions as a response to France's support for the Iranian people after the killing of protesters in Dey month. Barrot added that Paris proposed sanctions against individuals and entities linked to the IRGC to the EU following cyberattacks on more than 700 retail centers in France.

On Sunday, 24 Aban, the homes of five Bahá'í families in Semnan were searched and three individuals were arrested. Intelligence officers arrested Behfar Khanjani, Hesam Tabianian, and Zohreh Nikayin, and personal belongings and electronic equipment were confiscated. The residences of Leida Pirasteh and her husband, as well as Babak and Parvaneh Shabirian, were also searched.

The son of a 50-year-old Shush municipality worker says his father fell while working with a lift and suffered a brain injury. He claims the lift had no safety features and parts of its body were rotten.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that all enemy scenarios including war, assassination, and heliborne attacks must be thwarted and the armed forces are capable of handling them. He added that the enemy must be made to understand that the nation will not surrender to economic pressure, sanctions, assassination, or military attack. These statements were made on Monday, 25 Aban.

The Israeli army announced that in the Thursday attack on Nasser Hospital in the Gaza Strip, several members of Hamas's military wing were killed, one of whom participated in the abduction of Adina Moshe. The army said Hamas had presented the killed as civilians, but investigations show they were members of the military wing. The target of the attack was a room and floor of the hospital used by senior Hamas commanders as a military command center, where civilians were forbidden to enter.

A court in Bahrain on Tuesday, 25 Aban, sentenced 64 Shia citizens, including 57 clerics, to life imprisonment on charges related to "terrorism" and connections with the IRGC. Bahraini authorities accused the defendants of "forming a terrorist group, cooperating with the IRGC, and attempting to overthrow the ruling system" of the country.

Amir Ghalenoei, head coach of Iran's national football team, criticized the short interval between matches and the condition of the playing field before the match against Iraq in the Basra international tournament, stating that the main goal of the national team is youth development, not achieving results. Ghalenoei said the interval between Iran's match with Palestine and the match with Iraq is shorter than the interval between Iraq's match with Lebanon and their match with Iran, which prevents the team from having proper tactical training. He also pointed out that holding two matches in one day on the same field will negatively affect the second match.

Carlo Ancelotti, the coach of Brazil's national team, responded to Romario's call for his dismissal by saying that Romario talks a lot but has the right to express his opinion. Ancelotti admitted that his team's performance is not yet satisfactory and emphasized that the team is in the phase of testing new players. He expressed satisfaction with the evaluation of players such as Gabriel Bontempo, Andre, and Jonathan Jesus.

Jean-Noël Barrot, France's Foreign Minister, said he will present evidence of Iran's involvement in cyberattacks on French store refrigerators to European diplomats. He hopes new sanctions against Iran for these attacks will be approved in mid-December. Iran's Foreign Ministry and the Revolutionary Guards deny the accusations and call it a false flag operation by Israel.

Alireza Zakani, mayor of Tehran, announced that in over five years, not a single meeting has been held to address the capital's air pollution problem. He emphasized that 23 agencies are involved in the air pollution issue and the municipality is only one of them. Zakani attributed the responsibility for holding meetings to other institutions and said a major part of Tehran's air pollution comes from activities around the capital.

Reuters reported, citing Iraqi officials, that Kata'ib Hezbollah, one of the most powerful armed groups supported by the Islamic Republic in Iraq, has earned hundreds of millions of dollars through an oil smuggling network. According to security and oil officials, this network has operated since 2021 with the cooperation of some government officials, and investigations have led to the dismissal of 9 senior officials. Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, has ordered the deployment of more forces around the Jurf al-Sakhar area.
Mahnaz Ebrahimi, a math teacher and teachers' union activist in Shiraz, was released from Adelabad prison in Shiraz on Sunday, 24 Aban, on bail. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The war in Iran and disruptions in oil tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz have cast a shadow over the ASEAN summit in Manila. Eleven Southeast Asian countries and their partners face rising energy and transportation costs and demand guarantees for the safe passage of ships through this route.

Some viewers of Iran International said the suppression of protesters in Aban 98 ended their hope for reforming the Islamic Republic. Others said the experience deepened their opposition to the government. Viewers mentioned internet shutdowns, shooting protesters, arrests, and commemorated the martyrs of Aban.

The director general of forensic medicine in Semnan province announced that from the beginning of this year until the end of Mehr, 236 people died and 4255 were injured in traffic accidents in this province. The number of injured increased by 2% and the number of deaths by 11% compared to the same period last year. Among the deceased, 207 died in intercity accidents, 23 in urban accidents, and six on rural roads.

A video sent to Iran International shows a large presence of security motorcyclists on Neshat Street in Isfahan on Tuesday, 25 Aban. According to reports, the area of this street has been heavily secured with checkpoints and armed individuals.

Mohammad Sajjad Shahdoust, a detainee related to the December 1404 protests, is serving his two-year sentence in Tehran Grand Prison. He was transferred to prison on 16 Aban. The Revolutionary Court sentenced him on charges of "disturbing public order" and "propaganda against the regime."

Zohreh Sadat Lajevardi, Tehran's parliamentary representative, said that women's motorcycling is "not our main priority" and that livelihood problems and the situation of female heads of households should be addressed. She added that issuing licenses for women's motorcycling should be examined considering its "requirements" such as potential dangers and how women dress while motorcycling.

Alireza Dabir told Fars news agency that those who asked why forces go to Syria now understand the reason for their presence. He said the city council allocated a budget in 1386 for building Iranian Park in southern Lebanon and discussed the spending with Qasem Soleimani. According to Dabir, Soleimani laughed and said 3 billion tomans is a small amount because the forces stand for Iran.

The government of Pakistan announced that Shehbaz Sharif, the Prime Minister of the country, met in Islamabad with foreign ministers and heads of delegations of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) member countries, including Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic. These officials traveled to Pakistan to attend the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Ministers. Additionally, Muhammad Ishaq Dar, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, held a bilateral meeting with Abbas Araghchi and emphasized that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only practical solution to resolve remaining issues, prevent escalation of tensions, and achieve lasting peace and stability.

In the eighth week of the Iranian Women's Premier Football League, Khatoon Bam defeated Persepolis 4-1. Despite this loss, Persepolis remained at the top of the table with 18 points. Esteghlal, Gol Gohar, Sepahan, and Varesh also won their matches.

Mahbubeh Ramazani, mother of Pejman Gholipour, who was killed in Aban 98, said she had no hope from the beginning for the investigation of the complaint regarding the murder of her 18-year-old son in the Islamic Republic. She added that the Islamic Republic arrests families of the killed to force them into silence. Ramazani said she is proud that her son gave his life for the freedom of Iran.

Mohammed Al-Khalifi, Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, called for strengthening guarantees to protect mediating countries, the security of negotiators, and confidentiality of diplomatic talks at the Future Resilience Forum in London. He described mediation as both an international responsibility and a national interest, highlighting Qatar's role in prisoner exchanges between the US and Venezuela and support for Colombia's peace process. Al-Khalifi also emphasized the importance of countries' credibility and ability to connect conflicting parties.
A released video shows that after rainfall on Monday, 25 Aban, flooding occurred on the ring road of Nowshahr city in Mazandaran province.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced that the Islamic Republic launched between 8,000 and 9,000 suicide drones and about 2,000 ballistic missiles since the start of the "Epic Anger" operation. He said only three of these drones and missiles caused American casualties. Trump described the defensive performance of the US Central Command as effective and historic.

Alireza Esteghamati, head of the Medical School at Tehran University of Medical Sciences, said the cost of diabetes treatment in Iran has increased nearly sixfold in one year. The rise in drug and equipment prices and insurance problems have made access to treatment more difficult for patients. Mehdi Beigi in today's supplement has examined the dimensions of the diabetes crisis in Iran and its consequences.
Trump said he is worried about the reporter because if he is targeted by Iranian drones, the reporter will also be harmed. He warned the reporter to be careful.

Donald Trump announced that he will discuss Iran, the Ukraine war, and nuclear disarmament in meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. He also mentioned the possibility of meeting with the North Korean leader. Trump spoke about the difficulty of nuclear disarmament and the possibility of listing the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization in the US.

Mohammad Sharifimoghaddam, Secretary-General of the Nurses' House, identified staff shortages, work pressure, and livelihood problems as major factors in nurses' job burnout. He said some nurses have to care for 12 to 15 patients and during night shifts 25 to 30 patients. He also criticized the lack of a comprehensive system for monitoring nurses' physical and mental health, with consequences such as anxiety and depression.

According to a video received by Iran International, a municipal worker in the city of Shush, Khuzestan province, fell while working with a lift. In this video, recorded by the injured worker's child, the poor safety condition of the municipality's equipment and lift is highlighted.

Simultaneous with the arrival of the third US aircraft carrier near Iran, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament said Iran is on the brink of war. Also, on Sunday night, the Israeli security cabinet held a three-hour meeting with the presence of the Mossad chief about an attack on Iran.

Kaja Kallas, EU foreign policy chief, said in a November 16 press conference that cyberattacks in France indicate Europe is also targeted by Iran, and the EU is preparing more sanctions. She made these remarks regarding the Russia-Ukraine war, developments in Syria, and regional security issues. Kallas warned about Iran's reach into European countries and announced preparations for additional sanctions.

It was reported that from the beginning of Farvardin to 21 Mehr 1405, at least 84 women and girls have been killed in Iran. In 75 cases, the perpetrator was an acquaintance of the victim, and in 45 cases, the perpetrator was identified as the current or former husband, ex-husband, or romantic partner. Additionally, 12 of the victims were girls under 18 years old.

Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old student from Gilan-e Gharb living in Kermanshah, was killed by her father on Sunday, 24 Aban. The Hengaw Human Rights Organization reported that the cause of the killing was the father's opposition to Sogand's relationship with her suitor. The management of Rezvan Girls' High School in Kermanshah summoned Sogand's father to the school one day before the murder and he severely beat his daughter in the presence of classmates and school officials.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, stated in a conversation with Nabih Berri, the Speaker of the Lebanese Parliament, that the Islamic Republic pays special attention to Lebanon in pursuing its demands and conditions in the negotiation process. Ghalibaf said that from their perspective, without ending the war in Lebanon and achieving Lebanon's sovereignty over its territories, peace will not return to the region.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, met with Mohammad Nasir Akhund, the Taliban's Finance Minister, in Tehran. According to domestic news agencies, the two sides discussed regional issues. These talks took place while Afghanistan has become one of Iran's most important trade and transit routes.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said Paris has been targeted by the IRGC because of its support for the Iranian people; an institution that he said the European Union considers a terrorist organization. Barrot added that France will not forget the "widespread crimes" of the IRGC against Iranians in Dey 1404.

China's Foreign Ministry announced that Xi Jinping, the President of China, will have a trilateral meeting with the leaders of the United States and Russia on Thursday in Shenzhen. It is expected that the Ukraine war, Middle East developments, Iran war, trade policies, and nuclear non-proliferation will be on the agenda of these talks. This will be the first trilateral meeting of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin.

The Israeli army announced that its air force targeted a shipment of weapons and military equipment destined for Hezbollah in the Janta area on the Syria-Lebanon border. The army stated that the purpose of this attack was to prevent the strengthening of Hezbollah's military capabilities.
A released video shows the mother of Mohsen Abbasi expressing longing for her son by holding his clothes. Mohsen Abbasi, 21 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Najafabad.
